prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system. Mission: continuous potable water meeting regulatory and demand targets, with operator visibility, automatic control and manual intervention. Boundary: River Intake Pump Station and Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment, disinfection, storage to High Service Pump Header. Aliases: - Ironwood = River Intake Pump Station. Normally automatic; demand and channel depth govern starts. Permissives: suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips. Start blocked if Screen Channel level below low limit, drive fault, local control, or interlock unproven. Lost permissive: alarm or stop by severity. - Lantern = SCADA Historian Server: stores trends (river level, screen differential, pump status, raw-water quality) for compliance and incident reconstruction. - Marigold = Coagulant Dosing Skid: meters primary coagulant automatically; sends Alum Batch Ticket when new chemical lot enters service. Dose trimming uses analyzer feedback, operator targets and verified response, not a single instrument. - Cobalt = North Filter Gallery: gravity filters; records each filter's effluent turbidity and headloss each control scan. Elements: - Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot after each cleaning cycle; rising differential = blinding; high-high level needs field confirmation. - South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note when run ends outside limits. - Filter runs managed on run time, terminal headloss, effluent turbidity, prior backwash quality, upstream condition. Washed filter returns only when rinse-to-waste meets target and turbidity stable. Unusual rise: compare analyzer with samples before declaring upset. - Clearwell Level Controller: watched during intake restrictions (main storage buffer). - Chlorine Contact Basin; Backwash Recovery Tank; Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench; High Service Pump Header. Actors: - Chief Operator: authority over modes, targets, abnormal response; authorizes Storm Intake Mode and return to normal after stabilization period; sets starting coagulant dose (turbidity, color, alkalinity, pH, temperature, bench tests); confirms sustained control point. - Duty Engineer: configuration control; reviews storm forecasts; may authorize temporary dose adjustment on rapid turbidity change. - Laboratory Technician: confirmation testing, incl. analyzer/filter disagreement; prioritizes storm raw-water checks. - Distribution Dispatcher: sends demand changes; notified when intake limits threaten Header meeting demand. - Maintenance Planner: post-storm intake inspection/cleaning scheduling. - Chemical Supplier Driver; Residuals

New part:
S066: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is used for custody-controlled receipt of compliance and process samples collected from treatment locations.
S067: The SCADA Historian Server retains dose changes, analyzer values, filter status changes, wash sequences, and operator comments for later review.
S068: Manual override is permitted for chemical feed, valve sequencing, and filter start or stop actions only when automatic control is unavailable or inappropriate for the condition.
S069: An operator placing equipment in manual control is expected to state the reason, monitor the affected process variable closely, and restore automatic control as soon as practicable.
S070: Manual chemical feed changes are made in small increments unless an immediate water-quality risk requires a larger correction approved by the Chief Operator.
S071: If analyzer feedback is lost, operating staff hold the last verified safe dose or revert to an approved fixed dose while collecting additional grab samples.
S072: A sustained loss of coagulation effectiveness is treated as a process deviation and prompts review of chemical strength, feed pump status, mixing energy, and raw-water characteristics.
S073: The Chlorine Contact Basin is considered in the response because excessive particulate carryover can affect downstream disinfectant demand and contact performance.
S074: The Clearwell Level Controller remains coordinated with filter production so that filter shutdowns, backwashes, and return-to-service decisions do not create avoidable storage swings.
S075: When filter capacity is reduced, the Distribution Dispatcher is advised of expected production limits before changes affect the High Service Pump Header.
S076: After any significant deviation, the Chief Operator reviews trends from the affected operating period and confirms that corrective actions restored stable clarified and filtered water quality.
S077: Following operating deviations, laboratory sampling provides independent confirmation that treatment targets have returned to acceptable control ranges.
S078: The Chief Operator establishes daily sampling priorities based on plant conditions, regulatory monitoring requirements, and recent process adjustments.
S079: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is also known as Sparrow for local bench labeling during sample receipt.
S080: Field samples are labeled at collection with location, time, collector initials, preservation method, and requested analyses before they leave operating areas.
S081: The Laboratory Technician checks container type, holding time, temperature, preservative status, and seal condition before logging a sample for analysis.
S082: Samples from the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Chlorine Contact Basin, and High Service Pump Header are verified against the current sampling schedule before testing begins.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
